The Twenty Point Programme (TPP) was formulated as a composite poverty alleviation

project in 1975 and was restructured in 1982, 1986 and 2006. Now it is renamed as “Twenty Point Programme 2006”.

The main objective of the Programme is to eradicate poverty and improve the quality of life of the poor and under-privileged population. Vi.

Guidelines towards the implementation of Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme

Scheme Rationale:-

Women education and literacy plays a vital role for any socio economic development of the State. The gender Gap in the literacy rate of higher education / the less enrolment ratio of girl children, percentage of girl children from Government schools enrolment in higher education has been analysed. Various steps have been taken for motivating the girl children to pursue their higher education.

Scheme Design:-

Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme is a Conditional Cash Transfer that concentrates on girl students who have completed their 6" — 12" Std education in Government/department schools and who pursue their higher education in educational institutions recognized by Government of Tamil Nadu / Government of India / University Grants Commission and situated in Tamil Nadu for all recognized courses of Under Graduation, Paramedical courses, Diplomas and ITI courses etc.

Conditional Cash Transfer as incentive:

The scheme provide a cash benefit of Rs.1,000/- per month to be paid monthly to the girl student on DBT mode who have completed their gh _ 42™ Std in Government schools provided that she is enrolled in any of the higher education ‘institution recognized by the Government of Tamil Nadu / Government of India / University Grants Commission and situated in Tamil Nadu.

The term higher education encompasses any recognized under graduation course of 3 years / 4 years / 5 years / combined PG course / Diploma / ITI certificate course for one/two or three year courses in all streams.

Salient features of the scheme

By making financial benefits, conditional upon the girl students, this programme negotiate a behavioral change in the area of higher incidences of early marriage and low ratio of enrolment in higher education, and retention of girl students in higher education. Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme therefore envisages empowerment of girls specifically who have passed out from Government schools.

i Promotes girl students educational status and instill motivation to pursue higher education giving them better foundation in both economic and social spheres including improving gender parity at higher levels.

ii. | Enables the creation and participation of skilled women workforce.

ABSTRACT

Home Department - Prisons - Implementation of a new scheme “Seerthirutha Siragugal” for the reformation and rehabilitation of all types of prisoners —Financial sanction — Accorded - Orders - Issued.

Home (Prisons-III) Department

2. From the Director General of Police/ Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services, Chennai, letter No.16358/PW3/2022, dated 02.03.2023.

ORDER:-

In the Government Order first read above, Government have accorded administrative sanction for recurring expenditure of a sum of Rs.100.00 lakh only towards implementation of a new scheme “Seerthirutha Siragugal” for the reformation and rehabilitation of all types of prisoners. In the said Government Order the Director General of Police/Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services was requested to send a separate proposal for financial sanction for the above amount along with break up details for the same to Government at appropriate time.

2. In the letter second read above, the Director General of Police/Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services has sent the revised proposal to Government to implement the scheme “Seerthirutha Siragugal” for the financial year 2023-2024 wherein, he has stated that Prison and Correctional Services departments implemented a lot of reformation programmes in_ prisons all

over Tamil Nadu. Education, skill training, industrial training, yoga, meditation etc are a few mention. However, most of these programmes mainly concentrate on convict prisoners whose population is very less i.e., 30% of the total prison population when compared with remand/undertrial prisoners and recidivism rate is also very high among the under trials rather than convict. Hence, there is an absolute necessity to implement correctional programmes among those groups and the correctional programmes which are run by this department does not cater to the need of all kinds of prisoners. Hence, the Government of Tamil Nadu has announced a scheme called “Seerthirutha Siragugal” in order to convert the prisons as reform centres with a holistic approach.

3. The Director General of Police/Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services has further stated that while talking about the correctional programmes to all kinds of prisoners, first and foremost thing is reforming the attitude of the inmates without which no rehabilitation could be done. At this juncture, it is pertinent to note that the substance abuse and drug addiction is the driving force of crime indulgence. So, it becomes vital to overcome this obstacle in the reformation process. Creation of De-addiction Centres in prisons thus emerges as a necessity.
